subject: Optimize Toolkit pricing: batching, KV-cache & quantization runway
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma@stellarlabs.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stellarlabs.com
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask: Optimize Toolkit crediting + technical recs

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the product overview today. We liked the demo of the Optimize toolkit (especially the batching/caching dashboard). Before we take this to procurement, a couple of asks so we can model costs and internal sign-off: 

1) For a 3-month pilot (low volume, ~3M tokens/month) what does a typical credit/commit shape look like if we want to try KV-cache + 4-bit quantization? Any recommended guardrails?

2) Does Redwood recommend enabling continuous KV caching across sessions for our use case (customer support retrieval + short context chat)? Any SLO tradeoffs?

3) Are there standard commercial concessions for pilots where we need custom autoscale rules (we target predictable burst capacity during business hours)?

Can you send a short worksheet and any technical constraints we should highlight for our infra/security reviewers.

Appreciate it — Emma
Emma Stone
Head of ML Products | Stellar Labs
emma@stellarlabs.com

Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, procurement@stellarlabs.com
Date: 2026-06-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: Optimize Toolkit crediting + technical recs

Hi Emma —

Great questions — I pulled together a short note and a worksheet (attached) that maps pilot sizing to credit shapes and the recommended runtime knobs. High level:

- Pilot proposal: 3 months, 3M tokens/month baseline. Recommend a two-part credit: 100% covered baseline credits for predictable volume + a small burst buffer (10–15%) that can be consumed and reconciled monthly.
- KV-cache guidance: For support retrieval + short chat, enabling persistent KV cache with a 24–48 hour TTL gives the best cost win without materially impacting latency SLOs. If sessions are extremely short-lived (<30s), the win is marginal.
- Quantization: 4-bit (q4) recommended for the majority of request types; keep unquantized for hallucination-sensitive generation (fine-tune paths). We can scope a mixed runtime: q4 for inference, fp16 fallback for critical routes.
- Commercial: For pilots we typically offer a 20–30% pilot credit on hosted tokens + waived setup for custom autoscale rules; we can firm exact % after a short tech validation.

Connor will follow up with specific latency numbers and an ops checklist. Kimberly will outline any procurement redlines we've seen.

Next step: quick sync Friday to review worksheet and draft SOW? 

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: "redwood_quant_recs.pdf" (summary, PDF)

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-20T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick latency/ops numbers for Stellar pilot (notes)

Evelyn / Kim —

Notes for Friday call with Stellar:
- Baseline config: gpt-like open model (redwood-3b-opt), q4 quant, batching target 8–16 concurrently (per-GPU). Expected median token latency: 50–80ms on Dedicated A100 equiv for typical 128-token responses.
- KV-cache: enabling 24h TTL reduces token compute ~25–40% depending on prompt overlap. Cold-start penalty for first request ~20–30ms.
- Autoscale: to honor daytime bursts (2–3x baseline), suggest reserved baseline vCPU/GPU pool + burst nodes with warmup policy (keep 1 warm node per zone).
- Observability: we will surface token breakdown by route, so they can see cost delta for quant vs fp16.

Caveats: q4 can subtly change sampling behavior for long-form generation — we'll recommend an eval set (10–20 prompts) to validate quality before enabling across customer-facing flows.

Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Emma Stone <emma@stellarlabs.com>, procurement@stellarlabs.com
Date: 2026-06-21T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: Optimize Toolkit crediting + technical recs

Emma / Team —

Quick procurement note so your legal/procurement folks can prepare:
- Standard pilot commercial: 3-month commitment letter (no long-term lock), hosted pricing with token credits applied monthly. Pilot credits would be documented as a rebate line on invoice.
- SLA & security: pilots run on Redwood Hosted in our us-west region by default; if Stellar requires VPC/Private control plane there is a one-time setup fee (we can waive for strategic pilots).
- Discounting: we can extend a one-time pilot concession of 25% gross credits (applied to baseline tokens) plus a capped burst buffer. If they convert to Reserved/Dedicated within 6 months we will apply an additional conversion credit.
- Redlines we anticipate: data residency language (we use encrypted-at-rest and SOC2 controls), and a standard indemnity carveout for model outputs — we typically handle that with a limited-liability clause rather than model-level warranty.

I'll drop the procurement checklist to the Drive link after this.

- Kim
Senior Dir, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what our finance team needs. A couple quick clarifications before Friday's sync: 

- Can you put the 25% pilot concession and burst buffer in the worksheet as an example row so our procurement team sees the math?
- For the eval set, we'll send 15 representative prompts this afternoon (mix of retrieval + generation). Please confirm whether we should expect any measurable quality delta on those prompts if q4 is enabled by default.
- Can you include a short note on how rollback to fp16 is handled (tech path + timeline)? We need to tell product how fast we can flip for customer-facing flows.

If those are in the worksheet, we're good to run this past procurement and get the signed commitment letter. Meeting Friday 10am PT works for us.
